subQuestions.questionText:
The map area shown on the 1:50 000 topographic map of Hermanus (3419 AC) falls within the … province.

A Eastern Cape
B KwaZulu-Natal
C Western Cape
D Northern Cape
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (Western Cape) (1 mark)
Hermanus is a coastal town in the Overberg region of the Western Cape Province. The topographic map 3419AC covers the Walker Bay coastal area in the Western Cape. Recognising which province a map falls in is a basic orientation skill tested in mapwork.

subQuestions.questionText:
The type of rainfall experienced in the Hermanus area shown on the map is …

A convectional
B orographic
C frontal
D relief
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (frontal) (1 mark)
The Western Cape, including Hermanus, experiences a Mediterranean climate characterised by frontal (cyclonic) rainfall in winter, brought by cold fronts tracking across from the southwest. Convectional rainfall dominates the interior and eastern regions of South Africa in summer. Orographic and relief rainfall both refer to air being forced over mountains, which is not the primary mechanism at Hermanus.

subQuestions.questionText:
The height above sea level at a fixed survey point is precisely shown on the topographic map by means of a …

A contour line
B benchmark
C spot height
D trigonometric beacon
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (benchmark) (1 mark)
A benchmark (BM) is a precisely levelled survey point permanently marked on the ground and recorded on the topographic map with its exact altitude above mean sea level. Spot heights indicate approximate heights at specific points but are less precise. Contour lines show general height bands. Trigonometric beacons (trig beacons) are for horizontal positioning, not altitude benchmarking.
subQuestions.topic: Mapwork: Map Skills — Height and Relief

subQuestions.questionText:
The Leeurivier on the map flows in a/an … direction.

A northerly
B easterly
C north-westerly
D south-westerly
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (northerly) OR C (north-westerly) — both answers accepted (1 mark)
On the topographic map of Hermanus, the Leeurivier flows northerly or north-westerly from its source in the mountains towards the lower-lying coastal areas. Rivers always flow from high to low ground; the contour patterns on the map confirm a northerly or north-westerly flow direction. Both A and C are accepted in the official marking guidelines.

subQuestions.questionText:
Use the line scale to calculate the straight-line distance between point A and point B on the map extract. The distance is …

A 1 200 m
B 2 400 m
C 3 600 m
D 4 800 m
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 400 m) (1 mark)
Using the line scale, the straight-line distance between points A and B is 2 400 m (2.4 km). Method: measure the distance between A and B with a ruler in millimetres, then compare this against the line scale on the map to convert to the ground distance. On a 1:50 000 map, 1 mm on the map = 50 m on the ground.

subQuestions.questionText:
Using the map, determine the true bearing from the place of worship to the school. The true bearing is approximately …

A 055°
B 125°
C 235°
D 315°
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (235°) (1 mark)
A true bearing is measured clockwise from True North (0°/360°). A bearing of 235° places the school in a south-westerly direction from the place of worship. Method: draw a north-pointing line at the place of worship, then measure the angle clockwise to the line connecting the place of worship to the school. A bearing of 235° is between S (180°) and W (270°), confirming a south-west direction.

subQuestions.questionText:
The man-made feature indicated by number 3 on the orthophoto is a …

A communication tower
B water tower
C church steeple
D lookout tower
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (communication tower) (1 mark)
The structure at location 3 on the orthophoto is a communication tower (radio/cell mast), identifiable by its tall, slender lattice or tubular steel structure. Communication towers are used to transmit radio, television, and mobile phone signals. They are typically found on elevated ground to maximise signal coverage.

subQuestions.questionText:
The orchards and vineyards at location M are situated on the …

A north-facing slope
B south-facing slope
C valley floor
D upper mountain slope
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (valley floor) (1 mark)
The orchards and vineyards at location M are situated on the valley floor near the river. Valley floors in the Western Cape provide fertile alluvial soils deposited by river action, easy access to irrigation water from the river, and a relatively sheltered microclimate. These conditions make valley floors highly suitable for intensive fruit and vine cultivation.
subQuestions.topic: Mapwork: Topographic Map Interpretation — Vegetation and Agriculture

subQuestions.questionText:
The high-lying ground between two river valleys at location N is known as a/an …

A ridge
B interfluve
C plateau
D escarpment
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (interfluve) (1 mark)
An interfluve is the elevated ridge of land that separates two adjacent river valleys or drainage basins. At location N, the high-lying ground divides the drainage systems on either side. An escarpment is a steep cliff face; a plateau is a large flat elevated area; a ridge is a long narrow elevated feature — but in the specific context of land between river valleys, the correct geographical term is interfluve.
subQuestions.topic: Mapwork: Geomorphology — Drainage and Relief Features

subQuestions.questionText:
The streams in block D8 show evidence of mainly … taking place.

A vertical erosion
B lateral erosion
C deposition
D delta formation
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (vertical erosion) (1 mark)
The streams in block D8 are in the upper course of their journey, where steep gradients give the water high energy. This energy is used for vertical (downward) erosion, deepening the river channel into a V-shaped valley. Lateral (sideways) erosion and deposition are more characteristic of the middle and lower course where gradients are gentler and the river has more water volume.
subQuestions.topic: Mapwork: Drainage — River Erosion and Deposition

subQuestions.questionText:
The drainage pattern visible in block H8 is …

A radial
B trellis
C parallel
D dendritic
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (dendritic) (1 mark)
A dendritic drainage pattern resembles the branching structure of a tree, with tributaries joining the main stream at acute angles in an irregular branching network. It develops in areas where the underlying rock is uniform in hardness and structure. The pattern in block H8 shows this characteristic tree-like branching. A radial pattern drains outward from a central high point; trellis has tributaries meeting at right angles; parallel has streams flowing in the same direction.

subQuestions.questionText:
The activity in block B5 that is causing environmental damage is …

A deforestation
B urbanisation
C cultivation
D excavations
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (excavations) (1 mark)
The visible diggings/excavations in block B5 represent quarrying or mining activity. Excavations destabilise the land surface, destroy vegetation and topsoil, expose bare rock and sediment to erosion, and can contaminate water sources. This makes excavations a significant cause of environmental damage in this area.

subQuestions.questionText:
The MAIN physical factor that has determined the dispersed settlement pattern at location 4 is the …

A steep gradient
B distance from the coast
C lack of water sources
D poor soil quality
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (steep gradient) (1 mark)
The dispersed (scattered) settlement pattern at location 4 is primarily caused by the steep gradient of the terrain. On steeply sloping ground, flat buildable land is limited and found only in pockets, so dwellings are placed far apart wherever suitable flat ground exists. This results in a dispersed rather than a nucleated or clustered settlement pattern.

subQuestions.questionText:
The LINEAR shape of the built-up area in blocks J10, K9 and K10 is mainly due to the …

A railway line running along the coast
B mountains and rocky coastline
C availability of commercial fishing
D flat terrain between the sea and the highway
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (mountains and rocky coastline) (1 mark)
The linear (ribbon-like) shape of the built-up area along the coast in blocks J10, K9 and K10 is caused by the physical constraints of mountains on the inland side and the rocky coastline on the seaward side. These two barriers squeeze urban development into a narrow corridor, forcing the settlement to extend linearly along the coast rather than spreading inland.

options.A: railway line running along the coast
options.D: flat terrain between the sea and the highway

subQuestions.questionText:
The MAIN function of the New Harbour area indicated by number 5 on the map is …

A primary
B secondary
C tertiary
D quaternary
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (tertiary) (1 mark)
Tertiary activities are service-based activities that involve the provision of services to consumers and businesses. New Harbour at location 5 is associated with fishing-related services, boat maintenance, fish markets, and tourism activities such as whale watching — all of which are tertiary (service) functions. Primary activities involve extracting raw materials; secondary involves manufacturing/processing; quaternary involves information and knowledge-based activities.
